Target VSIPL uses vsip_cscalar_f struct with .r/.i and separate split-plane views, VSIP_MEM_NONE created complex vector views. Important semantic delta: vsip_cvdot_f conjugates the second operand, unlike a plain dot product. In target they used an explicit loop for the FIR complex convolution instead of cvdot, presumably to avoid conjugate and split-plane dot products. That's a key pitfall: mapping a plain dot product to a library's conjugate-dot routine flips the sign of imaginary parts.

title: "Streaming complex mix-and-decimate channelizer rebuilt from block vendor DSP primitives onto a view-based signal-processing API"

when_to_use: When a real-time streaming spectral layer (NCO mixer + decimating complex FIR + per-block output statistics) is built on a vendor block-kernel library (vector primitives that operate on interleaved complex buffers and return status codes) and must move to a view-based signal processing API whose complex samples are struct scalars and whose arrays are accessed through created views with element put/get. Match conventions: caller-owned split real/imaginary planes in the public ABI, streaming state across calls, block-size-independent output, allocation ownership of internal history/scratch.

mapping_rules (each one decision, source concept -> target mechanism with condition/fallback):

1. Interleaved complex scalar with adjacent real/imaginary members → complex scalar constructor paired with an accessor per component; when target exposes named constructors and component accessors, build and take apart scalars explicitly instead of casting between the two layouts, because the source interleaved layout is not a documented target layout. Fallback: if the target kernel accepts a paired-plane buffer signature, skip scalar construction entirely and pass the split planes.
2. Split real/imaginary planes → keep split planes as the internal and public representation; only materialize a complex object where a target routine requires a complex argument (e.g. per-sample multiply or a view element). Applies when the public ABI already splits planes; if the caller's ABI uses interleaved arrays, create one interleaved view and copy in/out.
3. Elementwise complex multiply kernel over a contiguous run (with a windowed coefficient offset) → per-sample complex multiply in a segment loop bounded by the coefficient table length; keep the segment loop and phase carry so the coefficient window wraps at block boundaries. Applies when target has no in-place complex multiply over a strided run; fallback: use the target's elementwise complex view multiply on a temporary contiguous view.
4. Plain (non-conjugating) real dot product over a run → explicit accumulation loop in the required order, or the target's complex/real dot routine only if it does not conjugate an operand. Condition: target dot products that conjugate their second operand must not be used where a plain correlation is required. Fallback: explicit loop.
5. Coefficient time reversal: source stored coefficients reversed to match a forward dot-product walk; target keeps coefficients in natural order and walks history backwards. Rule: the orientation decision belongs to one place — pick forward-walk-with-reversed-coefficients or backward-walk-with-natural-coefficients, never both, and verify with a direct-form reference. Also: the reference/validation coefficients are given in natural (causal) order; hidden reversal conventions in a state struct are a classic port defect.
6. Vendor memory allocation/free for internal buffers → standard heap allocation/free (or the target library's memory-flag-created views). Who allocates: the module allocates its own state and internal history/scratch, copies caller-provided coefficient and NCO tables at create time (borrows during the call, does not retain pointers), and frees everything in destroy. Target views created by the module are owned by the module and destroyed explicitly. Condition: if the target library's create routines allocate and return a view, ownership follows the view and the data must not be freed separately.
7. Per-sample statistics: sum of |x|^2 and max |x| → create a complex view over the output block, take magnitudes into a real view, ask the target for the maximum value and its index; accumulate the mean power from the split planes so it is computed in one pass (avoid summing squared magnitudes). Condition: only when the target provides vector magnitude and index-of-max reduction. Fallback: plain loop with strict greater-than comparison (keeps the first index on ties).
8. Status-returning kernel calls → routines that report failure by NULL/void; validity checks and error returns stay in the module's own guards. When the target reports errors by returning a NULL object for create and by returning nothing for compute calls, the module must validate arguments and check every created view for NULL itself. Fallback: if the target has an error-query API, read it at the same points.
9. Timed-vector/math-link build wiring: compile the backend sources against the target include dir and link the static library plus the math library; the source backend option was an explicit define + shared vendor libs. Condition: build system chooses one backend source set; no both-backends link.

def _derive_id(title: str) -> str:
    """Derive a stable id from the card title.

    Titles are human-facing and may be non-ASCII; fall back to a short digest
    so every component still has a stable identifier.  An over-long title is
    cut at a word boundary and tagged with a short digest, never mid-word.
    """
    slug = _SLUG_RE.sub("-", title.strip().lower()).strip("-.")
    slug = re.sub(r"-{2,}", "-", slug).strip("-.")
    if len(slug) < 3:
        return "component-" + hashlib.sha1(title.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]
    if len(slug) <= 64:
        return slug
    suffix = "-" + hashlib.sha1(slug.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]
    head = slug[: 64 - len(suffix)]
    cut = head.rsplit("-", 1)[0].strip("-.")
    if len(cut) < 24:
        cut = head.strip("-.")
    return cut + suffix


def normalize_transformation(
    value: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    example: dict[str, Any],
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Normalize one agent-produced transformation into the internal shape."""
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise ValueError("transformation must be an object")
    status = str(value.get("status") or "draft_ready").strip().lower()
    if status not in STATUSES:
        raise ValueError(f"transformation status must be one of {sorted(STATUSES)}")
    title = _text(value.get("title"), "title", minimum=5, maximum=None)
    # Identity is deterministic: the pipeline names every component from its
    # title.  A model-supplied id is ignored so a repair cannot rename a family.
    transformation_id = _derive_id(title)
    when_to_use = _text(value.get("when_to_use"), "when_to_use", minimum=20, maximum=None)
    mapping_rules = _text_list(value.get("mapping_rules"), "mapping_rules")
    semantic_deltas = _text_list(value.get("semantic_deltas"), "semantic_deltas")
    pitfalls = _text_list(value.get("pitfalls"), "pitfalls")
    procedure = _text_list(value.get("procedure"), "procedure")
    verification = _text_list(value.get("verification"), "verification")
    boundary = _text(value.get("boundary"), "boundary", minimum=20, maximum=None)
    applicability = _applicability(
        value.get("applicability"), os_values=_target_os(example)
    )
    evidence = _evidence(value.get("evidence"))
    capability = _capability_from_example(example)

    # The corpus provenance is authoritative: always attach it so a component
    # cannot claim a migration it was not extracted from.
    source_meta = example.get("source") or {}
    project = str(source_meta.get("repo") or "").rsplit("/", 1)[-1].removesuffix(".git")
    canonical = {
        "project": project,
        "commit": str(source_meta.get("commit") or ""),
        "task_id": str(example.get("task_id") or ""),
        "role": "source-migration",
    }
    if not any(
        item["project"].lower() == canonical["project"].lower()
        and item["task_id"] == canonical["task_id"]
        and item["commit"] == canonical["commit"]
        for item in evidence
    ):
        evidence.insert(0, canonical)

    return {
        "schema": TRANSFORMATION_SCHEMA,
        "status": status,
        "transformation_id": transformation_id,
        "title": title,
        "capability": capability,
        "when_to_use": when_to_use,
        "mapping_rules": mapping_rules,
        "semantic_deltas": semantic_deltas,
        "pitfalls": pitfalls,
        "procedure": procedure,
        "verification": verification,
        "boundary": boundary,

    }


def _iter_strings(value: Any, path: str = "") -> Iterable[tuple[str, str]]:
    if isinstance(value, str):
        yield path, value
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for index, item in enumerate(value):
            yield from _iter_strings(item, f"{path}[{index}]")
    elif isinstance(value, dict):
        for key, item in value.items():
            yield from _iter_strings(item, f"{path}.{key}" if path else str(key))


def _flatten_text(value: Any) -> str:
    return " ".join(text for _, text in _iter_strings(value))


def _normalize_quote(value: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", value).strip().lower()


def field_text(transformation: dict[str, Any], field: str) -> str | None:
    """The searchable text of one card field; ``None`` for an unknown field."""
    if field not in CARD_FIELDS:
        return None
    return _flatten_text(transformation.get(field))

- **Layout**: keep the ABI's split real/imaginary planes; build complex scalars only where a per-sample call needs one; drop the source's interleaved scratch and its lifetime bookkeeping. Fallback to a contiguous complex view when a target routine demands interleaved data.
- **Arithmetic**: segment loop bounded by the coefficient-table length with the phase carried in state (block-size-independent output); plain accumulation loop wherever the target's inner product conjugates an operand.
- **Orientation**: natural-order coefficients with backward history walk instead of a reversed coefficient copy plus forward dot product — one orientation decision per layer, pinned to a direct-form reference.
- **Ownership**: module allocates state/history/scratch, copies caller tables at create, releases everything on every failure branch; target view storage is owned by the view and freed only through its destroy call.
- **Errors**: no target per-call error channel, so argument guards and NULL checks on created views stay in the module.

Also captured: last-bit re-association deltas, peak tie-breaking, alignment loss versus the vendor allocator, unset report fields on the failure branch, per-call view leaks, plane/interleaved stride confusion, and backend-define build drift — with direct-form, block-split, report, failure-path and sanitizer checks that an unprivileged process can run.
